Tomato___Early_blight.description: A common fungal leaf disease that can reduce plant vigor.
symptoms: Brown spots that may form concentric rings
Lower leaves often show symptoms first
recommended_actions: Remove and dispose of visibly affected plant material
Improve airflow and avoid wetting foliage when watering
Use an appropriate registered treatment according to its label and local agricultural guidance
prevention: Use clean tools and disease-free planting material
precautions: Do not apply chemicals contrary to product labels
Consult a local agricultural expert for a confirmed diagnosis
Tomato___Early_blight.disclaimer: This is AI-assisted screening information, not a professional diagnosis.

Potato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease that commonly affects older potato foliage and may reduce yield when severe.
symptoms: Dark brown leaf spots, often with concentric rings
Yellowing around spots and gradual drying of affected leaves
Symptoms often begin on older, lower leaves and can spread upward
recommended_actions: Remove and dispose of heavily affected foliage where practical
Avoid overhead watering and allow foliage to dry
Ask a local agricultural expert whether a locally registered treatment is appropriate
prevention: Rotate potatoes with non-host crops and avoid planting potatoes in the same area repeatedly
Use healthy seed potatoes and remove volunteer potato plants and crop debris
Maintain suitable spacing and monitor lower leaves regularly
precautions: Do not apply chemicals contrary to product labels
Confirm the diagnosis with a local agricultural expert, as other problems can look similar
Potato___Early_blight.disclaimer: This is AI-assisted screening information, not a professional diagnosis.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal leaf disease that often begins on lower, older tomato leaves. Visual screening can confuse it with other leaf spot diseases.
symptoms: Small, round, dark spots on lower leaves
Spots may develop pale gray or tan centers with tiny dark specks
Affected leaves may yellow, dry, and fall prematurely
recommended_actions: Remove spotted lower leaves when practical, without removing more than one-third of the plant's foliage
Water at the base of the plant and avoid handling wet foliage
Ask a local agricultural expert to confirm the cause before considering treatment
prevention: Stake or trellis plants and provide good spacing for airflow
Mulch beneath plants to reduce soil and debris splashing onto lower leaves
Rotate tomatoes and peppers away from the same location for two years where practical
Remove diseased plant debris and do not save seed from affected plants
precautions: Other tomato leaf spot diseases can look similar; this AI result is not a confirmed diagnosis
Use any pesticide only if locally registered for tomatoes and strictly according to its label
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.disclaimer: AI-assisted screening information, not a professional diagnosis.
